newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods flat amid absence of trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods flat amid absence of trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices remained flat early Friday as an absence of trade left the market indifferent to minor weakness in energy futures trade.
No deals were reported early Friday, traders said, as the market cleared out ahead of next week's Christmas holiday.
"It'll be very thin trade," next week, a trader said.

NYMEX January gasoline fell about 1.22 cents in late New York trade. It followed heating oil's fall of about 0.98 cents amid news Saudi Arabia might not need to cut its oil production if the United Nations lifts sanctions against Iraq.
January conventional unleaded gasoline was flat, ranging 72/73 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, while CARB-grade stayed held at 74.50/76 cents.
Jet fuel was flat 76.50/77.50 cents in L.A.
